correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact 3x3 Gram density (det G)^((d-4)/2) over positive-definite matrices with each diagonal <1, including the normalization I_d=(8*pi^(3/2)/d^3)*Gamma((d-1)/2)*Gamma((d-2)/2)/Gamma(d/2)^2 from the three radial-square integrals and two beta correlation integrals. The obtuse linear inequality is F(G)=G11-G12-G13+G23<0. The positive definite maximizer G* with diagonals 1, offdiagonals (1/3,1/3,-1/3) has determinant 16/27 and inverse as specified; logdet concavity and its supporting gradient give a strict global saddle under F<=0 and Gii<=1. Independently symbolically expanded the full determinant in the six scaled marks: linear h coefficient zero; second-order coefficient exactly -(3/2)(z+u+v)-Q(t,p,q)/2 for h=1/sqrt(d). The 3x3 Gaussian Hessian has determinant 2187/64 and parent T variance 8/9, while the one-sided constraints z,u,v have rate 3/4 in the (d-4)/2 exponent. Local boundary Laplace integration gives the single-vertex constant sqrt(6)/12, multiplied by three disjoint obtuse vertices to sqrt(6)/4. Strict global localization plus the local dominating Gaussian/exponential envelope make the transformed conditional densities L1-convergent and hence total-variation convergent by Scheffe. Numerical finite-d simulations and importance tests supplement but do not prove the asymptotic. The support uses volume-uniform balls, not sphere-surface uniform sampling.

originality.rationale: PASS as to the specifically claimed conditional six-coordinate marked law within the checked source body, with material historical-priority risk. Hall (1982) already gives an all-dimension exact integral for the marginal acute probability (thus could imply the leading probability after asymptotics), and is explicitly credited. Its accessible abstract does not specify the conditional Gram-variable boundary layer; its complete four-page paper was unavailable even after lawful publisher/OA routes, and authorized institutional retrieval reported disconnected VPN; no whole-document absence claim is made. The related sphere-surface Resultary theorem has a d^(-1/2) prefactor and no radial marks; the Gaussian-triangle conditional law is a different vertex distribution. Generic Laplace/Gram methods are tools, not claimed original.
residual_risks: Hall (1982) is a directly relevant four-page primary source whose complete text was not obtained; Oxford authorized retrieval returned vpn_disconnected, not a demonstrated NOT_COVERING.

The marginal probability constant might be derivable from the previously known all-d probability integral; novelty judgment rests on the joint six-mark total variation theorem, not isolated marginal asymptotics.

value.rationale: PASS: a full conditional rare-event geometry law explains the physical configurations generating a rare obtuse angle, beyond a marginal integral or leading exponent. The half-normal d^-1/2 deficit at the obtuse vertex, d^-1 exponential deficits at other vertices and the correlated inner-product Gaussian block demonstrate a distinctive mixed-scale boundary mechanism. Total-variation convergence is stronger than a basic moment or weak-limit computation and is a motivated exact shape limit.

final_claim: For three independent volume-uniform points in the d-dimensional unit ball, P(obtuse triangle) is asymptotic to (sqrt(6)/4)(16/27)^(d/2). Conditioned on an obtuse angle at one labelled vertex, six explicitly normalized Gram-coordinate marks converge jointly in total variation to a half-normal/Gaussian/exponential product law with stated variances and rates.
limitations: Only independently volume-uniform samples in unit Euclidean d-balls; dimension tends to infinity; conditional finite real Gram coordinates, not ambient vectors; no finite-d quantitative convergence rate.
